answer: One concrete defense is superlinear identity fees. Each agent must bond funds to register, and the fee scales with the square of identities tied to one shared funding kernel. An honest agent pays once; a sybil swarm flooding the ocean of accounts from a single source hits quadratic cost: 1,000 fakes cost ~1,000,000 units, not 1,000. Attackers try splitting funding across wallets to dodge this, so the network also weights trust by an attestation signal from established peers, leaving cheap fresh identities economically worthless.
